summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS resolver for the shared 10.100.215.0/24 network: it answers inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.215.11) via a system static-host-mapping consumed by pdns-recursor, and forwards all other queries upstream to 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9. node2 and node3 (RHEL7) were reconfigured via nmcli (ipv4.dns=10.100.215.10, ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes) to resolve exclusively through node1. Verified inventory.internal and external resolution work end-to-end from node2 and node3. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health, issued native reboot, confirmed connection drop, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified DNS config/resolution health post-restart before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes: node1 is VyOS 2026.04.02-rolling; node2/node3 are RHEL 7.9 using NetworkManager DHCP, previously pointed at platform gateway 10.100.215.1

On node1: configured service dns forwarding (listen-address 10.100.215.10, allow-from 10.100.215.0/24, name-servers 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9) and system static-host-mapping for inventory.internal -> 10.100.215.11; committed and saved
Verified node1 answers inventory.internal authoritatively (10.100.215.11) and forwards external queries (example.com) via dig against 10.100.215.10
On node2 and node3: used sudo nmcli to set ipv4.dns=10.100.215.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes on the eth0 connection, reactivated it, confirmed /etc/resolv.conf updated to nameserver 10.100.215.10
Verified inventory.internal and example.com resolve correctly from node2 and node3 through node1
Captured baseline boot_id and service/data health on all 3 nodes before any restarts

Restarted node1 via sudo reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified pdns-recursor active plus inventory.internal/example.com resolution
Restarted node2 via sudo reboot, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified resolv.conf and DNS resolution through node1 persisted
Restarted node3 via sudo reboot, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified resolv.conf and DNS resolution through node1 persisted

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DNS resolver forwarding upstream
evidence.summary: Set service dns forwarding on node1 (listen 10.100.215.10, upstream 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9) and static-host-mapping; dig against node1 returned inventory.internal=10.100.215.11 and resolved example.com via upstream
dig on node1 and getent hosts on node2/node3 all show inventory.internal -> 10.100.215.11 (node2's address)

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1
evidence.summary: nmcli set ipv4.dns=10.100.215.10 on both nodes; resolv.conf shows nameserver 10.100.215.10; getent hosts confirms internal and external resolution working through node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebd78841...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; connection timed out confirming reboot in progress; post-reboot boot_id changed to f98a86d3...; pdns-recursor active and DNS resolution (internal+external) working again

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3dba43a5...; reboot acknowledged; SSH connection timed out confirming reboot; post-reboot boot_id changed to 987d215e...; resolv.conf and DNS resolution (inventory.internal + example.com) confirmed working post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 738d0aac...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 4cfa6b2d...; resolv.conf and DNS resolution (inventory.internal + example.com) confirmed working post-reboot
